boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Brandeis University
boards.description: When the library closes or the midnight hunger hits, Brandeis students rely on a mix of campus staples and Waltham's legendary Moody Street corridor for late-night fuel.

cards.title: The Hoot Market
cards.subtitle: Lower Usdan Student Center
cards.notes: Grab snacks and essentials at this campus convenience store, which stays open until 2:00 AM daily during the semester.
cards.short_summary: The primary on-campus destination for late-night snacks and dorm supplies.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hoot Market is open Monday – Friday 9:30 am – 2:00 am and Saturday – Sunday 10:30 am – 2:00 am.
cards.source_title: Dining Locations – Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM daily during the academic year.

cards.title: The Stein
cards.subtitle: Hassenfeld Conference Center
cards.notes: Visit this historic campus pub for burgers and shareables; it serves as a social hub with hours extending to midnight.
cards.short_summary: A campus restaurant and social space offering late-night dining and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stein is open Thursday – Sunday from 5:00 pm – 12:00 am.
cards.source_title: Dining Locations – Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight Thursday through Sunday.

cards.title: Shapiro Campus Center
cards.subtitle: Central Campus
cards.notes: Access 24-hour study spaces and lounges in the SCC using your Brandeis ID for late-night productivity.
cards.short_summary: The main student union building offering 24/7 card access for studying and student activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Shapiro Campus Center (SCC) is card-accessible 24 hours for students.
cards.source_title: Visiting Student Engagement Spaces - Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Card access available 24/7 for current students.

cards.title: Einstein Bros. Bagels
cards.subtitle: Shapiro Campus Center
cards.notes: Stop by for coffee and bagels during late-night study sessions; it remains open until 10:00 PM on weekdays.
cards.short_summary: A popular spot for caffeine and snacks located inside the Shapiro Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Einstein Bros. Bagels is open Monday – Thursday until 10:00 pm and Sunday until 9:00 pm.
cards.source_title: Shapiro Campus Center - Brandeis Dining
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM Monday through Thursday.

cards.title: In A Pickle Restaurant
cards.subtitle: Moody Street
cards.notes: Head to Moody Street for creative burgers and wings; the kitchen serves its night menu until 10:00 PM.
cards.short_summary: A Waltham favorite known for its extensive breakfast and late-night wing menu.
cards.evidence_claim: In A Pickle is open Wednesday - Saturday until 10:00 pm, with wings exclusively available 3pm-10pm.
cards.source_title: In A Pickle Restaurant - Contact Us
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM Wednesday through Saturday.

cards.title: Shopper's Café
cards.subtitle: Moody Street
cards.notes: Visit this neighborhood pub for late-night food; the kitchen serves a full menu until 11:00 PM on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing Waltham pub offering late-night dining and a casual atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Shopper's Café kitchen is open until 11 PM Thursday - Saturday, with the bar open until 1 AM.
cards.source_title: Hours + Directions | Shopper's Cafe Waltham
cards.access_notes: Kitchen open until 11:00 PM Thursday through Saturday.

cards.title: Bistro 781
cards.subtitle: Moody Street
cards.notes: Enjoy new American cuisine at this Moody Street spot where the kitchen stays open until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: An upscale yet casual bistro offering late-night dinner options in downtown Waltham.
cards.evidence_claim: Bistro 781 serves dinner until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Hours + Location | Bistro 781
cards.access_notes: Dinner served until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday.

cards.title: Domino's Pizza
cards.subtitle: Lexington Street
cards.notes: The reliable choice for late-night delivery to campus, operating until 1:00 AM or later most nights.
cards.short_summary: A staple for late-night pizza delivery among Brandeis students.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's at 205 Lexington Street is open until 1:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: 205 Lexington Street in Waltham - Domino's Pizza
cards.access_notes: Open for delivery and carryout until 1:00 AM daily.

cards.title: BranVan Shuttle
cards.subtitle: Campus-Wide Service
cards.notes: Use the university's escort safety service for late-night transportation between campus buildings and Waltham stops.
cards.short_summary: The university's late-night shuttle and safety escort service.
cards.evidence_claim: The BranVan operates as an evening shuttle and safety escort service, with schedules extending past midnight.
cards.source_title: Campus Shuttles and Van Routes | Public Safety
cards.access_notes: Operates late-night hours during the academic semester; check TripShot app for live tracking.

cards.title: Incredible India
cards.subtitle: Moody Street
cards.notes: Order authentic Indian cuisine late into the evening at this successor to the legendary Little India on Moody Street.
cards.short_summary: A popular Indian restaurant on Moody Street offering late-night dining and delivery.
cards.evidence_claim: Incredible India (formerly Little India) at 475 Moody St offers late-night dining options.
cards.source_title: Incredible India - Gourmet Indian Restaurant
cards.access_notes: Check website for current seasonal late-night hours.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study nooks, quiet lounges, and specialized labs that Brandeis students use to navigate their academic and social lives beyond the standard admissions route.

cards.title: Farber Mezzanine Study Area
cards.subtitle: Above the Starbucks in Farber Library
cards.notes: Head up the stairs from the library Starbucks to find collaborative stations and team-spot desks ideal for group work with a social buzz.
cards.short_summary: A social, collaborative study level located directly above the campus Starbucks in Farber Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Farber Mezzanine contains collaborative stations and group study rooms and is located one floor above the Farber 1 Starbucks.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Brandeis Library
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; accessible via stairs or elevator from the Farber 1 entrance.

cards.title: The Quiet Floor
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Goldfarb Library
cards.notes: Retreat to the lowest level of Goldfarb for absolute silence; this floor is strictly designated for individual, distraction-free study.
cards.short_summary: The designated quietest floor in the library system, located two levels below the main entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Goldfarb 3 is officially designated as a quiet floor and houses study carrels for individual work.
cards.source_title: Library Maps | Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the main Goldfarb entrance; follow signs for Level 3.

cards.title: Mandel Center Roof Garden
cards.subtitle: Top floor of the Mandel Center for the Humanities
cards.notes: Visit the fourth floor to access the roof garden, a peaceful outdoor space for reading or quiet reflection with views of the campus.
cards.short_summary: An elevated outdoor garden space located on the top floor of the humanities center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mandel Center for the Humanities features a roof garden accessible to the campus community.
cards.source_title: A Center of Attention | Brandeis Magazine
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; take the elevator to the 4th floor.

cards.title: SCC Quiet Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Shapiro Campus Center Upper Floor
cards.notes: Use the MacBooks and individual desks in this sun-drenched lab for a quiet alternative to the often-busy main SCC atrium.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, window-lined computer lab on the upper level of the Shapiro Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The upper level of the Shapiro Campus Center features a computer lab with MacBooks and desks for quiet study.
cards.source_title: Andy's Best Study Spaces, Part 1 | The Heller School
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24 hours with a valid Brandeis ID card.

cards.title: Heller Breakout Rooms
cards.subtitle: Ground floor of the Heller-Schneider Building
cards.notes: Claim a first-come, first-served breakout room for private group meetings or focused individual work; each room includes a TV and chargers.
cards.short_summary: Private, tech-equipped rooms on the ground floor of the Heller School used for group study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Heller-Schneider building ground floor has several breakout rooms available for student use on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.source_title: On Campus Study Spots | The Heller School
cards.access_notes: Available to all students; rooms are first-come, first-served unless reserved for academic sessions.

cards.title: Gerstenzang Grad Lounge
cards.subtitle: Main floor of Gerstenzang Science Library
cards.notes: Relax in this casual lounge featuring a small kitchen, complimentary snacks, and sofas; it's a social hub for the science community.
cards.short_summary: A social lounge for graduate students located within the Gerstenzang Science Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gerstenzang Graduate Student Center provides a place to relax, socialize, and study with complimentary snacks.
cards.source_title: Spaces for Graduate Students | Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Primarily for graduate students; located on the main floor of the science library.

cards.title: Slosberg Music Practice Rooms
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Slosberg Music Center
cards.notes: Find a private room with a grand piano on the lower level; these are open to all Brandeis community members for practice.
cards.short_summary: Individual music practice rooms equipped with grand pianos, open to the entire campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Slosberg Music Center has practice rooms on the lower level open to all members of the Brandeis community on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.source_title: Practice Rooms | Department of Music
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; first-come, first-served for the general community.

cards.title: Shapiro Science Atrium
cards.subtitle: Main entrance of the Shapiro Science Center
cards.notes: Study in the bright, modern atrium overlooking campus; it offers ample seating and a professional atmosphere for science students.
cards.short_summary: A large, sunlit atrium with dedicated study spaces within the university's main science complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Shapiro Science Center features an atrium with study space and seminar areas.
cards.source_title: Campus Map | Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; accessible to all students.

cards.title: Kutz Hall Grad Center
cards.subtitle: First floor of Kutz Hall
cards.notes: Utilize the computers, scanners, and kitchen facilities in this dedicated grad space; it's a prime spot for social events and late-night work.
cards.short_summary: A comprehensive resource center for graduate students featuring study equipment and social spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Graduate Student Center in Kutz Hall includes computers, scanners, a refrigerator, and free snacks for graduate students.
cards.source_title: A grad student's guide to the best study spots at Brandeis
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Kutz Hall; primarily serves the graduate student population.

cards.title: Judaica Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Goldfarb Library Mezzanine
cards.notes: Find a quiet, traditional academic atmosphere in this specialized reading room; note that power outlets are limited here.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, specialized reading room on the mezzanine level of Goldfarb Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Goldfarb Mezzanine houses the Judaica Reading Room, which is used for quiet study.
cards.source_title: A Comprehensive Guide to Brandeis Study Spaces | Her Campus
cards.access_notes: Located on the Goldfarb Mezzanine; accessible via the main library entrance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore Brandeis University's best free social spots and activities, from world-class art galleries to serene campus trails and late-night student hubs.

cards.title: Browse Modern Masterpieces
cards.subtitle: Free Contemporary Art Gallery
cards.notes: Visit the museum's galleries to see rotating exhibitions of modern and contemporary art. Admission is always free for students and the public.
cards.short_summary: A premier contemporary art museum on campus offering free admission to all visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rose Art Museum is open to all with free admission and is committed to providing a respectful, safe, and inclusive experience.
cards.source_title: Hours and Admission | Visit | Rose Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday through Sunday, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

cards.title: Hang Out in the SCC Atrium
cards.subtitle: The Heart of Student Life
cards.notes: Relax on updated lounge furniture or meet friends in this central hub. It is card-accessible 24 hours a day for Brandeis students.
cards.short_summary: A central campus gathering space with 24-hour student access and comfortable lounge seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The SCC (the big green building by Fellows Garden) is also card-accessible 24 hours. There's a variety of seating options across all three floors.
cards.source_title: Shapiro Campus Center | Visiting Student Engagement Spaces
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours for students with valid ID swipe access.

cards.title: Hike the Sachar Woods Trails
cards.subtitle: On-Campus Nature Escape
cards.notes: Explore a mile-long network of dirt trails in the forest behind the International Business School. Look for the 'mysterious bench' for a quiet reading spot.
cards.short_summary: A wooded trail system on the edge of campus perfect for hiking and quiet reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Brandeis owns and maintains a little-known mile-long dirt trail network in the forest behind the International Business School.
cards.source_title: Sachar Woods Trail Map
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during daylight hours; located behind the IBS building.

cards.title: Work Out at Gosman
cards.subtitle: Free Student Fitness Access
cards.notes: Use the indoor pool, basketball courts, and weight room for free with your student ID. Check the schedule for open lap swim times.
cards.short_summary: A massive athletic complex offering free gym and pool access to all current Brandeis students.
cards.evidence_claim: All current Brandeis students, faculty, and staff, may use the athletic facilities free of charge. A valid Brandeis ID card must be presented.
cards.source_title: Facility Memberships and Guest Policies - Brandeis University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Open daily; typical hours are 7am-11pm Mon-Thu, with shorter weekend hours.

cards.title: Join a Shabbat Dinner
cards.subtitle: Weekly Community Meals
cards.notes: Experience a four-course gourmet dinner at the Chein family home. These weekly gatherings are open to all students regardless of observance level.
cards.short_summary: Weekly gourmet Shabbat dinners hosted for the student community at no cost.
cards.evidence_claim: Weekly gourmet Shabbat dinners... where students unwind, connect, and engage in meaningful conversations around the week's theme.
cards.source_title: Chabad House at Brandeis
cards.access_notes: Held weekly on Friday evenings; open to all Brandeis students.

cards.title: Stroll Through the Light of Reason
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Sculpture Garden
cards.notes: Walk through Chris Burden's installation of 24 Victorian lampposts outside the Rose Art Museum. It's a popular spot for photos and evening walks.
cards.short_summary: An iconic outdoor art installation featuring illuminated antique lampposts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Class of 2023 gathered at Chris Burden's 'Light of Reason' installation outside the Rose Art Museum for an annual tradition.
cards.source_title: First-years unite at Light the Night | BrandeisNOW
cards.access_notes: Outdoor installation accessible 24/7; lights are typically on in the evening.

cards.title: Reflect by the Three Chapels
cards.subtitle: Peaceful Waterside Spot
cards.notes: Sit by the pond adjacent to the Berlin, Bethlehem, and Harlan chapels. It is a quiet area ideal for meditation or reading between classes.
cards.short_summary: A serene pond area surrounded by the university's three interfaith chapels.
cards.evidence_claim: Located on Chapels Pond, adjacent to Chapels Field, the space is automatically open to all Brandeis students via swipe access.
cards.source_title: Catholic Chapel | Sacred Places | Center for Spiritual Life
cards.access_notes: Outdoor area open 24/7; chapels typically open 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. for students.

cards.title: Play Trivia at The Stein
cards.subtitle: Late Night Socializing
cards.notes: Join the weekly Trivia Thursdays from 9-11pm. It's a free social event where students compete in teams for bragging rights and fun.
cards.short_summary: A popular weekly trivia event held in the campus restaurant and social space.
cards.evidence_claim: Trivia Thursdays, 9-11pm, The Stein. Campus Programs and Traditions.
cards.source_title: Back to Brandeis and Winter Welcome | Campus Programs and Traditions
cards.access_notes: Trivia is held on Thursday nights; open to all students.

cards.title: Study with a View
cards.subtitle: Quiet Collaborative Space
cards.notes: Book a group study room or find a quiet corner on the mezzanine. It's a reliable spot for late-night productivity with easy access to resources.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated library level featuring group study rooms and individual workspaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Group study rooms are located on the Farber Mezzanine and on Goldfarb 1. Please use our booking page to reserve a group study room.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Rooms and Spaces | Library
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary; typically open until 2 a.m. most nights during the semester.

cards.title: Attend Mindful Moments
cards.subtitle: Weekly Guided Meditation
cards.notes: Join these half-hour meditation sessions led by staff and students. They are approachable, open to everyone, and designed to help de-stress.
cards.short_summary: Free weekly mindfulness and meditation sessions open to the entire campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Mindful Moments are half-hour gatherings that include staff- and student-led meditations, approachable and open to everyone on campus.
cards.source_title: Offerings and Events | Center for Spiritual Life
cards.access_notes: Weekly sessions; check the Center for Spiritual Life calendar for current times.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Discover ten distinct study environments at Brandeis University, from 24-hour student centers to quiet library mezzanines and specialized graduate lounges.

cards.title: Goldfarb Library Level 1
cards.subtitle: Collaborative Hub with Starbucks Access
cards.notes: Utilize large tables for group projects on the main floor. This level offers a casual atmosphere with easy access to the lower-level Starbucks for caffeine breaks.
cards.short_summary: A high-energy collaborative study area on the first floor of the main library.
cards.evidence_claim: Goldfarb 1 offers large study tables for group work and is located near the lower-level Starbucks.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Library - Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Open during standard library hours; Brandeis ID required for entry after certain hours.

cards.title: Farber Mezzanine Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Reservable Collaborative Spaces
cards.notes: Book a room for up to four hours daily. These spaces feature large tables and whiteboards, ideal for intensive group sessions and midterm preparation.
cards.short_summary: Private, reservable rooms equipped with whiteboards for student groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Group study rooms are located on the Farber Mezzanine and can be booked for up to four hours per person per day.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Library - Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via the library booking page; limited to 4 hours per day.

cards.title: Shapiro Campus Center Upper Level
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Quiet Zone with Natural Light
cards.notes: Find a quiet desk in the upper-level computer lab. Large windows provide natural light, and the building is accessible 24 hours a day with a student ID.
cards.short_summary: A bright, 24-hour study area located on the top floor of the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Shapiro Campus Center (SCC) is accessible by ID card 24 hours a day and features a quiet study space on the upper level.
cards.source_title: Shapiro Campus Center | Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 with a valid Brandeis ID card.

cards.title: Gerstenzang Science Library Quiet Area
cards.subtitle: Silent Study in the Science Complex
cards.notes: Head here for focused, silent study. This library provides a more traditional, quiet atmosphere compared to the social buzz of Goldfarb.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated silent study environment within the science library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Leo Gerstenzang Science Library provides a quiet place for study, ideal for exam preparation.
cards.source_title: A grad student's guide to the best study spots at Brandeis
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; check current library schedule for seasonal changes.

cards.title: Mandel Center Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Humanities Hub on the Third Floor
cards.notes: Visit Room 303 for a peaceful reading environment. This space is designed for small meetings and individual study within the humanities center.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading room located on the third floor of the Mandel Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of the Mandel Center contains a Reading Room (Room 303) available for community use.
cards.source_title: Academic Spaces | Mandel Center - Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Generally available during building hours; classrooms in the building are reservable after 6:45 PM.

cards.title: Heller School Breakout Rooms
cards.subtitle: Private Ground-Floor Workspaces
cards.notes: Use these first-come, first-served rooms for private meetings or online classes. Each room is equipped with chargers and a TV for screen sharing.
cards.short_summary: Ground-floor breakout rooms in the Heller-Schneider building for private study.
cards.evidence_claim: Heller School breakout rooms on the ground floor are available on a first-come, first-served basis and feature chargers and TVs.
cards.source_title: On Campus Study Spots - The Heller School
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served for students; public access typically M-F 7 AM-7 PM.

cards.title: Graduate Student Center (Kutz Hall)
cards.subtitle: Full-Service Lounge for Grads
cards.notes: Access computers, printers, and a kitchen with free snacks. This first-floor space in Kutz Hall is a dedicated hub for the graduate community.
cards.short_summary: A comprehensive study and social lounge for graduate students in Kutz Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Graduate Student Center in Kutz Hall offers computers, printers, a kitchen, and free snacks for graduate students.
cards.source_title: A grad student's guide to the best study spots at Brandeis
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduate students; located on the first floor of Kutz Hall.

cards.title: Peace Room (Usdan Student Center)
cards.subtitle: Quiet Reflection and Dialogue Space
cards.notes: Seek out this vibrant room for quiet reflection or small group dialogue. It is located on the first floor of the Usdan Student Center.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated space for quiet reflection and peacemaking dialogue in Usdan.
cards.evidence_claim: The Peace Room in Usdan is open to students for individual reflection or quiet during business hours.
cards.source_title: Peace Room | Center for Spiritual Life - Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Open during Usdan business hours; food and drink are not permitted.

cards.title: World Court (Lemberg Academic Center)
cards.subtitle: Open Atrium with International Flair
cards.notes: Study in this two-story open space lined with international flags. It offers a bright, airy environment for individual work between classes.
cards.short_summary: A scenic, flag-lined atrium in the International Business School building.
cards.evidence_claim: The World Court is an open space in the Lemberg Academic Center, typically open M-F 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.
cards.source_title: Spaces for Graduate Students | Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Typically open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM.

cards.title: Library Meditation Room
cards.subtitle: Silent Space for Mindfulness
cards.notes: Take a mental break in this room equipped with yoga mats and cushions. It is intended for meditation and finding a moment of peace during long study days.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet room for meditation and prayer within the main library.
cards.evidence_claim: The library's Meditation Room is intended for meditation, prayer, and mindfulness, with mats and cushions available.
cards.source_title: Rooms and Spaces | Library - Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; intended for silent use only.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Brandeis University, from the vibrant dining of Moody Street to the practical shopping hubs of Main Street.

cards.title: Dine on Restaurant Row
cards.subtitle: Moody Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk down Waltham's primary dining hub to find diverse international cuisine ranging from Cuban tapas to authentic Japanese ramen and local bakeries.
cards.short_summary: Moody Street is Waltham's central commercial corridor, famous for its dense concentration of independent restaurants and small shops.
cards.evidence_claim: Moody Street is known as 'Restaurant Row' and serves as the city's downtown hub with an international array of restaurants.
cards.source_title: About Waltham | Office of Graduate Affairs | Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7; most businesses open late morning through evening.

cards.title: Shop the Historic Center
cards.subtitle: Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the historic heart of Waltham for essential services, the public library, and a variety of cafes lining the route toward Watertown.
cards.short_summary: Main Street is a major east-west thoroughfare in Waltham featuring historic landmarks, government buildings, and retail centers.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street is lined with cafes, restaurants, venues, and businesses, serving as a key retail and transit corridor.
cards.source_title: About Waltham | Office of Graduate Affairs | Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; home to the Waltham Public Library and City Hall.

cards.title: Commute via the MBTA
cards.subtitle: South Street Corridor
cards.notes: Use this direct link between the Brandeis campus and the Brandeis/Roberts commuter rail station for easy access to Boston and Cambridge.
cards.short_summary: South Street is the primary road bordering the Brandeis campus, hosting the university's main entrance and the local commuter rail stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Brandeis University is located at 415 South Street, which borders the Brandeis/Roberts Station on the Fitchburg Line.
cards.source_title: Directions and Accommodations | Department of English | Brandeis University
cards.access_notes: Public road; the Brandeis/Roberts station is located directly on this street.

cards.title: Find Everyday Essentials
cards.subtitle: Lexington Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head north to find major shopping plazas featuring grocery stores, pharmacies, and quick-service dining options like Panera and Chipotle.
cards.short_summary: Lexington Street is a key commercial artery north of downtown Waltham, home to the Waltham Plaza shopping center.
cards.evidence_claim: Waltham Plaza at 1074 Lexington Street features Star Market, Panera Bread, and Chipotle, serving as a local stop for essentials.
cards.source_title: Waltham Plaza - Wilder
cards.access_notes: Commercial corridor; Star Market offers a 10% discount for college students during select months.

cards.title: Shop Sustainable Fashion
cards.subtitle: River Street Corridor
cards.notes: Browse gently-used clothing and accessories at Plato's Closet or visit the Shaw's supermarket for weekly grocery runs.
cards.short_summary: River Street runs parallel to the Charles River and hosts several large-scale retail stores and supermarkets.
cards.evidence_claim: Plato's Closet is located at 100 River Street and buys/sells clothes for young adults; Shaw's is also located on this corridor.
cards.source_title: Plato's Closet Waltham, MA
cards.access_notes: Retail area; Plato's Closet is open daily until 9 PM (6 PM on Sundays).

cards.title: Walk the Riverfront
cards.subtitle: Crescent Street Corridor
cards.notes: Access the scenic Charles River Riverwalk and find popular off-campus apartment complexes just blocks from the Moody Street bridge.
cards.short_summary: Crescent Street is a residential and recreational corridor along the Charles River, popular for student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Cronin's Landing at 35 Crescent Street offers a riverfront terrace and access to the tree-lined River Walk.
cards.source_title: Cronin's Landing - 35 Crescent St Waltham MA
cards.access_notes: Public riverwalk access; residential street.

cards.title: Play Mini Golf
cards.subtitle: Trapelo Road Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the newly opened recreation area for a round of seasonal mini golf or to explore the walking paths and open fields.
cards.short_summary: Trapelo Road is a major thoroughfare in North Waltham that hosts significant municipal recreation facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: 200 Trapelo Road features a universal playground, seasonal spray park, and seasonal mini golf.
cards.source_title: 200 Trapelo Road | Waltham, MA
cards.access_notes: Park open daily 9 AM - 7 PM; mini golf is seasonal.

cards.title: Hike Prospect Hill
cards.subtitle: Totten Pond Road Corridor
cards.notes: Access the trails of Prospect Hill Park for panoramic views of the Boston skyline from one of the highest points in the region.
cards.short_summary: Totten Pond Road provides access to Waltham's largest park and several residential communities.
cards.evidence_claim: Prospect Hill Park is located at 314 Totten Pond Road and offers miles of walking and cycling routes.
cards.source_title: Program Information | Waltham, MA
cards.access_notes: Public park access; trails are open dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Connect to Downtown
cards.subtitle: Prospect Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this connector to reach Hannaford Supermarket and CVS, or use it to bridge the gap between Main Street and the South Side.
cards.short_summary: Prospect Street is a vital connector road linking the northern and southern commercial districts of Waltham.
cards.evidence_claim: Prospect Street Apartments offer walking distance to Hannaford Supermarket, CVS, and numerous banks.
cards.source_title: Prospect Street Apartments - Capasso Realty
cards.access_notes: Public street; convenient for students living between campus and downtown.

cards.title: Explore Local History
cards.subtitle: Charles Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past historic multi-family homes and find the Charles River Museum of Industry & Innovation tucked just off this route.
cards.short_summary: Charles Street is a residential road that leads toward the historic mill district and the Charles River Museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Charles River Museum of Industry & Innovation is located at 154 Moody Street, accessible via the Charles Street area.
cards.source_title: Charles River Museum - Waltham
cards.access_notes: Public street; museum hours are typically Wednesday-Saturday.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From high-speed theater to body-paint choreography, Brandeis University's traditions reflect its creative and inclusive spirit.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Musical
cards.subtitle: A race against the clock in the Shapiro Campus Center
cards.notes: Audition, rehearse, and perform a full-scale musical in just 24 hours. The show title is revealed at 8 p.m. on Saturday, with the performance following on Sunday night.
cards.short_summary: A high-energy fall tradition where students produce a complete musical from scratch in exactly one day.
cards.evidence_claim: The 24-Hour Musical is a fall semester tradition at Brandeis organized by the Undergraduate Theater Collective where the show is announced and performed within 24 hours.
cards.source_title: Live theater returns with a Brandeis tradition: The 24-Hour Musical
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall at the Shapiro Campus Center theater.

cards.title: Liquid Latex
cards.subtitle: Wearable art on the Levin Ballroom stage
cards.notes: Watch or participate in a choreographed dance showcase where performers wear nothing but intricate designs made of liquid latex paint. It emphasizes body positivity and art.
cards.short_summary: A unique annual performance art show featuring students dancing in elaborate body paint designs.
cards.evidence_claim: Liquid Latex features Brandeis students dancing in latex paint and only latex paint, serving as a showcase of campus talent and creative expression.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Student Life | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the spring; tickets are often required for the showcase.

cards.title: Kindness Day
cards.subtitle: Spreading good vibes across campus
cards.notes: Join a day dedicated to small acts of thanks. Students exchange 'kindness cards' and participate in community-building activities to boost morale during the fall semester.
cards.short_summary: An annual November tradition focused on promoting community morale through small acts of kindness.
cards.evidence_claim: Kindness Day is an annual Brandeis tradition for more than a decade, packing as much kindness as possible into a single day every November.
cards.source_title: A few extra doses of kindness | BrandeisNOW
cards.access_notes: Campus-wide events held annually in November.

cards.title: Culture X
cards.subtitle: Multicultural revelry in Levin Ballroom
cards.notes: Experience one of the most popular shows on campus, where over a dozen student organizations collaborate for an evening of dance, poetry, and music celebrating global diversity.
cards.short_summary: The university's signature multicultural showcase featuring diverse creative expressions from student groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Culture X is an evening of multicultural revelry in the form of dance, music, and poetry, produced with the help of the Intercultural Center.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Student Life | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Held every April; popular event that often sells out.

cards.title: This Is Our House
cards.subtitle: Orientation slam poetry and spirit
cards.notes: Welcome the new class with this high-energy orientation event. It features slam poetry, hip-hop, and reflections on social justice to define the Brandeis community.
cards.short_summary: A spirited orientation tradition that introduces first-year students to the university's values through performance.
cards.evidence_claim: This Is Our House is an annual orientation event filled with slam poetry, school spirit, and reflections on social justice.
cards.source_title: First-years come together remotely for memorable This Is Our House
cards.access_notes: Primary event for incoming first-year students during orientation.

cards.title: Rubbing Louis's Toe
cards.subtitle: A lucky stride at Boston Rock
cards.notes: Rub the toe of the bronze Louis Brandeis statue for good luck on exams. The nine-foot figure captures the justice in mid-stride, robes flying in the wind.
cards.short_summary: A classic campus superstition involving the statue of the university's namesake.
cards.evidence_claim: The statue of Justice Louis Brandeis atop Boston Rock is an iconic campus landmark and the subject of student traditions.
cards.source_title: Louis Brandeis statue enlivens campus | BrandeisNOW
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors at Fellows Garden; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Library Hill Sled Races
cards.subtitle: Winter fun on the campus slopes
cards.notes: Grab a makeshift sled and head to the steep hill by the library after a heavy New England snowfall. It is a spontaneous but beloved winter rite of passage.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal tradition where students take advantage of the campus's hilly terrain for winter recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Library Hill Sled Races are listed as a unique Brandeis tradition by the Undergraduate Admissions office.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Student Life | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Spontaneous event occurring after significant snowfall.

cards.title: Springfest
cards.subtitle: The ultimate pre-finals concert
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of the academic year with a major outdoor concert on Chapels Field. Past performers include Kendrick Lamar and Childish Gambino.
cards.short_summary: The university's annual large-scale music festival held on the weekend before final exams.
cards.evidence_claim: Springfest is an annual concert held on Chapels Field the weekend before final exams, featuring major national acts.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Student Life | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Held annually in late April or early May; open to the Brandeis community.

cards.entity_name: Leonard Bernstein Festival of the Creative Arts
cards.title: Bernstein Festival
cards.subtitle: A creative tour de force
cards.notes: Honor the legacy of professor Leonard Bernstein with a week of immersive art, theater, and music. The campus transforms into a gallery and stage for hundreds of performers.
cards.short_summary: A massive annual arts festival celebrating the creative legacy of one of Brandeis's most famous faculty members.
cards.evidence_claim: Every April, Brandeis hosts the Leonard Bernstein Festival of the Creative Arts, an immersive showcase involving hundreds of students and faculty.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Student Life | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Held annually in April across various campus venues.

cards.title: Midnight Buffet
cards.subtitle: Late-night fuel for finals
cards.notes: Take a break from studying for a late-night feast provided by the Student Union. It is a high-energy gathering designed to relieve stress during the exam period.
cards.short_summary: A popular late-night dining event held during finals week to support students during exams.
cards.evidence_claim: The Midnight Buffet is a recurring large event organized by the Student Union for the student body.
cards.source_title: Midnight Buffet was a flop - The Brandeis Hoot
cards.access_notes: Typically held at midnight during finals week in the student centers.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Brandeis University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Arrive for Move-In Day
cards.subtitle: The start of your Brandeis journey
cards.notes: Pull into your assigned quad to meet Orientation Leaders who help unload your car and guide you to your new home.
cards.short_summary: New students arrive at Massell or North Quad to move into residence halls with help from student volunteers.
cards.evidence_claim: New Undergraduate Student Move-In typically occurs between 9am-1pm on the first Sunday of orientation at Massell or North Quad.
cards.source_title: Brandeis set to welcome record-breaking Class of 2022 for orientation
cards.access_notes: Move-in windows are assigned via the MyHousing portal; check-in is required upon arrival.

cards.title: Attend Convocation
cards.subtitle: Brandeis Beginnings ceremony
cards.notes: Gather on the grass for the official welcome ceremony featuring remarks from the University President and student leaders.
cards.short_summary: A formal welcome ceremony for new students and families held outdoors on Chapels Field.
cards.evidence_claim: Convocation: Brandeis Beginnings is held on Chapels Field as a brief ceremony to welcome new students and their families.
cards.source_title: Brandeis set to welcome record-breaking Class of 2022 for orientation
cards.access_notes: Open to all new students and their families during orientation weekend.

cards.title: Light the Night
cards.subtitle: A glowing orientation tradition
cards.notes: Join your classmates at Chris Burden's sculpture for a candlelit ceremony marking the start of your college career.
cards.short_summary: An annual orientation tradition where first-years gather at the Light of Reason sculpture for a candlelit ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Light the Night is an annual Brandeis tradition where students gather at the Light of Reason sculpture to commemorate the beginning of their journey.
cards.source_title: Scene at Brandeis: August 2025
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the evening on the first day of orientation.

cards.title: First Weekend Brunch
cards.subtitle: Fuel up at the dining hall
cards.notes: Enjoy a buffet-style brunch with new friends, featuring scratch-made pizza, a salad bar, and vegan options.
cards.short_summary: The main resident dining hall in Lower Usdan offering all-you-care-to-eat meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Usdan Kitchen provides buffet options for brunch/lunch and is a primary resident dining facility.
cards.source_title: Lower Usdan (Usdan Student Center) - Brandeis Dining
cards.access_notes: Requires a meal plan swipe or payment; open for brunch on weekends.

cards.title: Visit the Namesake
cards.subtitle: A campus landmark in Fellows Garden
cards.notes: Walk to the iconic bronze statue of Justice Louis Brandeis, depicted in mid-stride atop a rocky outcropping.
cards.short_summary: The iconic nine-foot bronze sculpture of Justice Louis Brandeis located in Fellows Garden.
cards.evidence_claim: The statue of Justice Louis Brandeis is located atop an outcropping in Fellows Garden and is a central campus landmark.
cards.source_title: Public Sculpture at Brandeis | Arts
cards.access_notes: Outdoors and accessible 24/7 in the center of campus.

cards.title: Explore Modern Art
cards.subtitle: Free admission for all
cards.notes: Wander through galleries of modern and contemporary art; don't miss the rotating exhibitions during the welcome open house.
cards.short_summary: A premier university art museum featuring modern and contemporary works, free to the public.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rose Art Museum is open to all with free admission and hosts a welcome open house for students in late August.
cards.source_title: Hours and Admission | Visit | Rose Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Galleries typically reopen in mid-August; admission is free for everyone.

cards.title: Find Your Community
cards.subtitle: The hub of student life
cards.notes: Stop by the SCC to browse the poster sale, visit club offices, or grab a coffee at Einstein Bros. Bagels.
cards.short_summary: The central student union building housing student organizations, lounge spaces, and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The Shapiro Campus Center (SCC) is the home of student engagement, club spaces, and Einstein Bros. Bagels.
cards.source_title: Shapiro Campus Center | Visiting Student Engagement Spaces
cards.access_notes: Open daily; Einstein Bros. Bagels has specific weekend hours (e.g., 10am-5pm Saturday).

cards.title: Ride into Waltham
cards.subtitle: Explore the local neighborhood
cards.notes: Show your Brandeis ID to board the free shuttle and head to Moody Street for local shops and restaurants.
cards.short_summary: A free shuttle service for students connecting the campus to downtown Waltham.
cards.evidence_claim: Brandeis provides free shuttle transportation to nearby Waltham; students must show their Brandeis ID to board.
cards.source_title: Shuttle Services | Transportation | Campus Services
cards.access_notes: Weekend combo routes run frequently; track real-time locations via the TripShot app.

cards.title: Get Active at Gosman
cards.subtitle: Athletics and recreation
cards.notes: Check out the fitness center or shoot some hoops in the Red Auerbach Arena to de-stress before classes start.
cards.short_summary: The primary indoor athletic facility at Brandeis, featuring a fitness center and multi-purpose courts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gosman Sports and Convocation Center houses the Red Auerbach Arena and fitness facilities for student use.
cards.source_title: FACILITY HOURS AND INFORMATION - Brandeis University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Brandeis students have access with ID; check seasonal hours for the weight room and arena.

cards.title: Late Night Snacks
cards.subtitle: Open until 2:00 AM
cards.notes: Grab a late-night snack or dorm essentials at this on-campus convenience store in Lower Usdan.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus convenience store in the Usdan Student Center offering snacks and essentials until late.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hoot Market is located in Lower Usdan and is open until 2:00 am daily, including weekends.
cards.source_title: Lower Usdan (Usdan Student Center) - Brandeis Dining
cards.access_notes: Open late night until 2:00 AM for snacks and beverages.
